decisions.decision: Midterm and make-up, both over chapters 1 to 8 (chapter 5, Debugging, now in); one 60-minute sitting; physical printed paper; one printed key per paper and form; this design is version 1.2.0 and replaces the single 30-item list of v1_1_0 by five questions.
decisions.reason: The Owner's instruction of 2026-11-01 13:04 (Istanbul) and the chapter list of the brief; v1_1_0 stays as committed and controlled.

decisions.decision: Page 1 is the İstanbul Kültür University (İKÜ) exam cover page, filled from the supplied template: department, course, exam kind, student name and identity number (ID) lines, academic year, term, date and time, duration, instructor, the grade table with rows Q1 to Q4, the bonus row Q5 and Total, the instructions, a row of learning outcomes per question, and the cheating warning. The generic parts are filled for SEN0414; the instructions are rewritten for an answer-sheet paper (nothing is written on the paper). The template itself is never stored in the repository.
decisions.reason: The Owner asked that the generic parts of the attached page be filled appropriately for each exam; the template is another course's document and must not be committed.

decisions.topic: Cover page: fields filled by the engine
decisions.decision: Course line from the course profile; instructor from the course outline (Yusuf Altunel); duration 60 minutes; academic year, term, date and time supplied by the Papers task as inputs (not guessed); learning outcomes per question from the outcomes file by the chapters of the question's sub-questions; program outcomes left empty with a printed dash because the repository has none (they are the department's, not the course's).
decisions.reason: No term, date or program-outcome fact is available in the repository; inventing them would break the rule against inventing facts. Marked A6 and A7.

decisions.decision: Q1 to Q4 are 25 points, Q5 is a 10-point bonus: base total 100, bonus up to 10. 30 sub-questions: Q1 6, Q2 7, Q3 7, Q4 6, Q5 4. Each question has one format.
decisions.reason: The Owner's wish (4 questions of 25, a fifth of 10, bonus) and the sub-question numbers of the brief.

decisions.decision: Read the program and predict: three predict (choose the printed output) and three mcq with a listing (choose the effect of a run). Points 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 5.
decisions.reason: Predict and mcq with a listing are the code-reading types kept in v1_1_0; the last is worth 5 because it combines two chapters.

decisions.decision: Complete the program: four blank gaps in one program and three cloze gaps in one explanation, each from its own option bank of at most 10 entries printed with two-digit codes. Points 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 3.
decisions.reason: Blank and cloze are the fill-in types kept; bank units hold at most 3 per block in the SEN0401 sheet, so 7 gaps give 3 blocks; the cloze asks WHY a construct exists, so it carries the reason questions.

decisions.decision: Choose the tool and say why it fits: a match block of five situations to seven lettered answers (3 points per premise) and two mcq on reasons (5 each).
decisions.reason: Match and mcq on reasons are the types the brief names; one premise is one sheet unit, so partial credit comes by premise.

decisions.decision: Order and effect: four printed steps are put in order (4 points per step) and two mcq on consequences (4 and 5).
decisions.reason: Order and mcq on consequences are the types the brief names; one step is one sheet unit (cells 1 to 4).

decisions.decision: Bonus across chapters: four mcq, two with a listing, that need two or more chapters or ask for a consequence, exception or reason. Points 3, 3, 2, 2.
decisions.reason: The brief names cross-chapter and indirect items; mcq is the only type that reads cleanly as an extra on the paper.

decisions.decision: A sub-question is the unit that is marked on the answer sheet: one choice row, one bank unit (a gap), one match premise or one order step. A match block of five premises is five sub-questions (3a to 3e); an order block of four steps is four sub-questions (4a to 4d). The form mark F is the 31st unit and is not a sub-question.
decisions.reason: The brief fixes 30 sub-questions with whole-number points and an answer sheet unit per sub-question; this is the only reading that gives 7 for Q3 (5 + 2) and 6 for Q4 (4 + 2). Marked A1.
The brief asks for whole numbers adding to the question total; heavier points go to the sub-questions that sit higher in Bloom's levels or combine chapters.

decisions.decision: Chapters 1 to 8 get 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 4, 4, 3 sub-questions (= 30). The lineage agent's defaults 4, 5, 5, 5, 3, 4, 4, 3 add to 33, three too many; chapters 2, 3 and 4 each give up one.
decisions.reason: The defaults add to 33 and the paper has 30 sub-questions, so three must go; chapters 2, 3 and 4 had the largest defaults (5 each), and taking one from each makes chapters 1 to 4 equal at 4 and keeps the defaults of chapters 5, 6, 7 and 8. Marked A2.

decisions.decision: Every question touches several chapters (matrix in blueprint.chapter_matrix); chapter 5 is asked in Q2, Q3 and Q4 (debugging steps, tools, order of steps), never in Q1 or Q5.
decisions.reason: A spread stops one question becoming one chapter's test, and the debugging chapter fits the tool and order formats best. Marked A3.

decisions.decision: The 60 minutes must be enough: the rates of v1_1_0 section 5 are reused (derived per premise, step and gap by division), plus four allowances of this design: 10 s to read a tip, 30 s per question for its shared text, 120 s for the cover, 8 s per sheet unit. Total 2630 s = 73.1 per cent of 3600 s, within the 90 per cent rule (3240 s).
decisions.reason: The measure is reused as the brief demands; the allowances cover what the new paper adds (tips, cover, a sheet filled from a separate paper). The 8 s per unit is a guess that is NOT_MEASURED with students. Marked A5.

decisions.topic: Why the paper is shorter in time than v1_1_0
decisions.decision: 73 per cent of the sitting is planned (v1_1_0 planned 82 per cent) although the number of sub-questions is the same.
decisions.reason: Match premises, order steps and gaps are quick and are now counted as sub-questions; the spare time is kept as a reserve for reading the tips and for slower readers.

decisions.decision: No sub-question at Remember (level 1): 0 of 30. Levels: Understand 3, Apply 16, Analyze 9, Evaluate 2, Create 0. Apply and above 27 of 30 (the rule: majority); Analyze and above 11 of 30 (the rule: at least 8).
decisions.reason: The brief's rule, with Remember no longer allowed (N1). Create cannot be asked on a paper where nothing is written. Marked A4.

decisions.decision: Of the 100 base points, 91 are at Apply and above (the rule: at least 50) and 32 at Analyze and above; counted again in the check from the sub-question table.
decisions.reason: The Owner's emphasis on use and reason is also a weighting wish; a rule by item count alone could be met with cheap sub-questions, so the points are tested too.

decisions.decision: Every sub-question has a field asks: use (how a construct is used), reason (why it exists) or effect (what changes). Counts: use 13, reason 7, effect 10.
decisions.reason: N4 of the brief: no sub-question asks for a name, keyword, definition, signature or syntax detail; the Owner's last sentence is read as: not syntax trivia, why a construct exists and how it is used matter more than its name.

decisions.decision: Bloom level 1 is not allowed; an item that can be answered by recalling a name, keyword, definition, function signature or syntax detail fails the item check; the answer must follow from reading the code or the situation.
decisions.reason: N1 of the brief.

decisions.decision: Each sub-question has terms (the specific terms it uses, possibly none) and tip (a short phrase of at most 20 words printed with the stem, or a margin line, that says what the term means). If terms is not empty the tip is not empty; the correct answer never depends on knowing the term's name; the tip never repeats an option text.
decisions.reason: N2 of the brief: students are not forced to remember terminology, and are helped when a term is used.

decisions.topic: Abbreviations in full at first use (N3)
decisions.decision: The engine keeps a registry of short forms (short, full form) for the whole paper including the cover; in print order, the first occurrence of each short form must be the full form followed by the short form in brackets, e.g. 'integrated development environment (IDE)'. A scan of the assembled text fails the paper if any all-capital token of two or more letters, outside the registry's exceptions (option letters, form mark), appears before its expansion.
decisions.reason: N3 of the brief; the scan is a function of the design check with fixtures of known answer.

decisions.decision: The stem keeps the Owner's 10-to-30-word rule; the tip is not counted in the 30 words.
decisions.reason: N5 of the brief; a tip is a separate printed part, so a stem plus tip can run longer without breaking the rule on the stem.

decisions.decision: The item model of v1_1_0 (17 fields) gets five new fields: question (Q1 to Q5), sub (a, b, c, ...), tip, terms, asks. The item validator is extended by the next task (TK4_ItemRules2); this design only fixes the fields.
decisions.reason: The brief names these five fields; the validator v1_0_0 stays as committed and checks exactly 17 fields.

decisions.decision: The six kept types stay (mcq, predict, match, order, blank, cloze); the eleven dropped types stay dropped. Per question: Q1 predict and mcq; Q2 blank and cloze; Q3 match and mcq; Q4 order and mcq; Q5 mcq.
decisions.reason: The brief builds the formats from the six kept types.

decisions.decision: Page-interactive questions remain seeds only; every item passes the near-copy measure of v1_1_0 section 2.1 (04-assessment/exams/exam_nocopy_v1_0_0.py).
decisions.reason: The Owner's earlier decision that still holds.

decisions.decision: Six pages: cover, four pages of questions, one page of answer sheet. Four in total is not possible at a readable size.
decisions.reason: Estimated 302 lines against 224 available in two pages; see page_budget.why_not_four. The estimate is checked by the engine's measurement.

decisions.decision: Option layout first, code width second, spacing and margins third; the type size is never a lever.
decisions.reason: The Owner asked for better formatting and readability on 6 pages; the engine measures, and no text is squeezed below readable size.

decisions.decision: Paper as .docx converted by LibreOffice to PDF; pages read with pdfinfo; fill of the last question page read from the lowest text line; the sheet pages come from the module's layout. Word's own layout is NOT_MEASURED.
decisions.reason: The measure must be a tool run, not an estimate; the environment has soffice and pdfinfo. Word may differ, so a spare of 8 per cent is kept.

decisions.decision: The SEN0401 answer sheet module (sen0401_exam_answersheet_v1_0_0.py) and reader (v1_1_0) are reused unedited. Units: one per sub-question and the form mark F: 14 choice, 5 match, 4 order, 8 bank (7 gaps and F) = 31 units, measured 1 sheet page in the module's own layout.
decisions.reason: The brief and the coordinator's acceptance of 2026-11-01 (the reader needs exact bubble positions). Fewer units than v1_1_0 (54) because a gap, premise or step is now one sub-question, not three units per item.

decisions.decision: Units run in paper order Q1a ... Q5d after F; consecutive units of one kind form blocks of at most 5 (choice, match, order) or 3 (bank) closed by the module's left-blank row.
decisions.reason: The module groups consecutive units of one kind; paper order keeps the student's transfer simple.

decisions.decision: Q5 is reported on its own line; the paper's score is Q1 to Q4 (out of 100) plus Q5 (up to 10), so the highest mark is 110. Capping at 100 for the course grade is a separate decision of the Owner.
decisions.reason: The Owner wrote '100 plus up to 10 bonus'. Marked A8.

decisions.decision: One key per paper and form: an editable .docx for people (answer, points, reason, the tip and a note on the chapter for every sub-question) and a machine key (JSON with SHA-256 over its content) with answer and points of every sheet unit. The key is refused when kind, form or version differ from the form mark in unit F.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for the key as .docx; the machine key keeps the v1_1_0 rule of a digest-sealed key file.

decisions.decision: Paper A and B as .docx; key A and B as .docx; the machine keys as JSON; the answer sheet as one position-exact PDF with its layout file, built by the SEN0401 sheet module; no QTI, no interactive HTML.
decisions.reason: The brief.

decisions.decision: Forms A and B have the same structure: the type, points, Bloom level and sheet unit of every position are equal; B reorders sub-questions only within a question among positions of the same type, points and Bloom level (a position with its own points, such as Q1f, keeps its place), and reorders options; so one sheet layout serves both.
decisions.reason: Equal positions keep the key points and the sheet identical; reordering stops neighbours copying.

decisions.decision: Of the 14 choice sub-questions the keys are A 4, B 4, C 3, D 3 (differ by at most one); no letter is the key of three in a row; the match answers use A to G with five different letters.
decisions.reason: Same intent as v1_1_0 section 5 for a smaller number.

decisions.decision: The repository has critical points for chapters 1 to 4 and 6 to 8 only; chapter 5 has a question bank and a chapter-code manifest but no critical-points file. The 3 sub-questions that have chapter 5 as first chapter therefore cannot yet satisfy the item rule that links an item to a critical point. This design records the gap; it does not create the file.
decisions.reason: The item validator (R06, R07) needs the link; creating the critical points is another task (it needs the chapter 5 deck read), and inventing them would break the rules. See owner_decisions.open_gaps.

decisions.decision: The module prints the title SEN0401 answer sheet; the engine overprints the title line on the rendered PDF (a white box with the SEN0414 text) without editing the module, and a person looks at the result once.
decisions.reason: Carried from v1_1_0 question Q6 with the same default; the module cannot be edited. Marked A9.

decisions.decision: All files are new versions; v1_0_0 and v1_1_0 design, check and validator files stay.
decisions.reason: The rule of the executors.

item_types_kept.why: One letter A to D, a sheet row of kind choice, read by machine; about 60 s plain and 100 s with a short listing; also carries combination-of-statements, find-the-faulty-line (four line numbers) and compare-two-designs items.
Five premises to seven lettered answers A to G, one sheet unit of kind match per premise, a low guess rate and partial credit by premise, about 240 s.
Four steps or four code lines printed shuffled, one sheet unit of kind order per step with cells 1 to 4, partial credit by step, about 120 s.
A gap in a code listing filled from a shared bank of at most 10 printed two-digit codes, one sheet unit of kind bank per gap, about 90 s per item of three gaps.
A gap in a sentence about the course filled from a shared bank of at most 10 printed two-digit codes, one sheet unit of kind bank per gap, about 60 s per item.

The printed result of a short listing, answered by choosing one of four printed outputs (a sheet row of kind choice); the digit-and-sign form of v1.0.0 is dropped because the sheet has no unit for it; about 120 s.

item_types_dropped.why: Several ticks with a penalty make one item several marks and a scoring rule to learn; its idea survives as an mcq with combination options.
A 50 per cent chance of a right guess; its idea survives as an mcq asking which statement is true.
Needs a screen to edit and run the program; the task survives as an mcq about a numbered listing.
Needs a screen to run the code; writing code on paper is not enabled because no rubric or named marker exists.
Writing code on paper is not enabled: no marking rubric exists and handwritten code cannot be graded reliably by machine.
A typed free string compared with a key needs a screen and handwriting cannot be read by machine with certainty.
Needs a screen to show and explore a graph of the corpus.
Needs a screen to show and explore an object view.
Needs a live question to the corpus; cannot be answered on paper.
Needs a live endpoint to run a query; cannot be answered on paper.
A written answer marked by hand; the Owner decided on 2026-10-30 that nothing is written freely, and the recommended default of no short items means every answer is read by machine.

cover.source: a template supplied by the Owner (not stored in the repository; another course's document)
fields_filled: grade table: Q1 /25, Q2 /25, Q3 /25, Q4 /25, Q5 bonus /10, Total /100
instructions rewritten for the answer-sheet paper
cover.instructions_rewritten: Write your name and identity number (ID) on the cover; answer on the answer sheet only, nothing is marked on the paper; fill the bubbles completely; copy the two-digit form mark into box F; devices are not allowed; the five questions and the bonus are explained in one line each.

questions.question: Q1
questions.title: Read the program and predict
questions.format: Each sub-question shows a short program (at most 12 lines). The student reads it and chooses what it prints or does (predict), or chooses the effect of a run (mcq with a listing).
questions.stem_note: one shared program per two or three sub-questions

questions.question: Q2
questions.title: Complete the program
questions.format: One program with numbered gaps (blank) and one explanation with numbered gaps (cloze); the gaps are filled from a printed option bank, each entry printed with a two-digit code that the student writes into the sheet.
questions.stem_note: two shared texts, each with its own option bank of at most 10 entries

questions.question: Q3
questions.title: Choose the right tool and say why it fits
questions.format: Five situations are matched to seven lettered tools or reasons (A to G); two further sub-questions choose the reason why a tool fits.
questions.stem_note: one match block of five premises and seven answers; two stand-alone mcq

questions.question: Q4
questions.title: Find the effect of a change, or put the steps in order
questions.format: Four printed steps of a task are put in order (the place 1 to 4 of each step); two mcq ask what changes when a line or a setting is changed.
questions.stem_note: one order block of four steps; two stand-alone mcq

questions.question: Q5
questions.title: Bonus: across chapters
questions.format: Four mcq that need two or more chapters together or ask for a consequence, an exception or a reason.

item_fields.inherited: the 17 fields of exam_design_v1_1_0 section 2 (id, chapters, source, bloom, critical_point, course_point, seed_item, type, stem, listing, options_or_blanks, answer, points, reason, indirect_form, code_width, bank_id)

new.rule: the question the sub-question belongs to; its type must be allowed in that question's format
unique within the question, letters without gaps; the sheet unit number is the question digit and the letter (1a ... 5d)

new.values: text of at most 20 words, or none
new.rule: required when terms is not empty (N2); never equal to an option; not counted in the 10-to-30 words of the stem (N5)

new.values: list of the specific terms the sub-question uses; may be empty
new.rule: at most two per sub-question; each has a tip (N2); no term is the answer

changed_rules.points: the whole-number points of the sub-question table

item_fields.note: The validator (exam_item_check_v1_0_0.py) checks exactly 17 fields and stays; the extension is the task TK4_ItemRules2.

abbreviation_rule.registry: list of {short, full}; exceptions: the letters A to G and 1 to 4 of options, the form mark F, SEN0414 (a course code)
abbreviation_rule.scan: In print order over cover, instructions, stems, listings' comments, tips and options, find tokens of two or more capital letters; the first occurrence of each must be directly preceded by its full form and followed in brackets by the short form, or be the expansion itself

arithmetic.rates_source: Section 5 of exam_design_v1_1_0: mcq plain 60 s, mcq with code 100 s, predict 120 s; match 240 s per item of 5 premises = 48 s per premise; order 120 s per item of 4 steps = 30 s per step; blank 90 s per item of 3 gaps = 30 s per gap; cloze 60 s per item and 5 gaps in 2 items = 24 s per gap (all derived by division, none new).
arithmetic.allowances_note: New with the five-question paper and not in v1_1_0 (own values, assumption A5): 10 s to read a tip for each sub-question, 30 s to read the shared text of each question, 120 s for the cover and its instructions (includes copying the form mark), 8 s per sheet unit to mark the answer sheet (31 units).

page_budget.decision: 6 pages: the cover (page 1), four pages of questions (pages 2 to 5) and the answer sheet (page 6, one page, measured).

estimate_rows.name: Q1 three predict (19 lines) and three mcq with a listing (17 lines)
Q2 one program with four gaps, one text with three gaps, two option banks, seven tips
estimate_rows.basis: 43 lines of v1_1_0 for 5 blank and cloze items, plus 4 for two more gaps and 7 for the tips

estimate_rows.name: Q3 one match block (14 lines) and two plain mcq (7 lines each), three tips
Q4 one order block (10), one mcq with a listing (17), one plain mcq (7), tips
Q5 two plain mcq (7) and two mcq with a listing (17), four tips
headings of Q1 to Q5 (title, points, one instruction line)

page_budget.why_not_four: Four pages in total leave two pages of questions: 2 x 112 = 224 lines at the densest layout of v1_1_0 against about 302 lines needed, so the type would shrink to about 74 per cent of 10 point, i.e. under 7.5 point. The Owner's rule is 'fit with 6 pages but better formatting and readability' when 4 do not fit.

levers.rule: Four options of at most 30 characters each print two per line (A and B, then C and D); longer options print one per line.
levers.effect: saves up to 2 lines per mcq

levers.rule: A listing is declared 45 characters (one column) or 90 (both columns, a full-width box); lines are shortened, never wrapped.
levers.effect: a 45-wide listing sits beside its options

levers.rule: A blank line before each sub-question; margins 12 mm, not below 10 mm; keep-together on each sub-question and its tip.
levers.effect: readability; 96 lines per page instead of 112

page_budget.never_levers: Body text below 10 point, code below 9 point, shading, a sub-question split over two pages, the sheet squeezed. These are not used to win a page.

measure.tool: The engine builds the paper as .docx, converts it with LibreOffice (soffice --headless --convert-to pdf) in a scratch folder and reads the page count with pdfinfo; the fill of the last question page is read from the lowest text line of that page (pdftotext -bbox).
measure.pass_rule: Cover + question pages = 5 and the last question page at most 92 per cent full (spare of one block for the difference between LibreOffice and Word); the sheet is 1 page by the module's own layout. Then the total is 6.
measure.fail_rule: More than 4 question pages is a FAIL of the layout: levers are applied in their order; if still over, the engine stops and reports, it never shrinks the type.
measure.not_measured: How Word lays the same .docx out is NOT_MEASURED (LibreOffice is the measure); the printed result must be looked at once by a person.

answer_sheet.layout: The sheet is the SEN0401 sheet module (sen0401_exam_answersheet_v1_0_0.py) and its reader (sen0401_exam_answersheet_v1_1_0.py), reused and never edited. A4 portrait, a header on the first page (title, form code, identification box, six printed rules), then blocks of at most 5 choice, match or order units or 3 bank units, each with a header row of option labels, one row per unit (two for a bank unit) with the number at both ends, and a closure row; blocks are flowed into two columns per page. The engine writes a layout file giving every row and bubble position; the reader reads that file and does not guess.
answer_sheet.mark_style: Fill the bubble completely in dark ink; X through a bubble withdraws it; one filled bubble without an X per row; fill the closure bubble of every number left blank; fill-in codes are two digits.

geometry.corner_marks: four L-shaped marks on every sheet page, leg 8 mm, stroke 1.2 mm, 7 mm from the page edges, no hollow marker

answer_sheet.student_id_line: An identification box in the header, filled by hand, read by a person only; no name or number printed; example sheets are synthetic.
answer_sheet.version_mark: The header prints a form code of four digits and a check digit from the specification; the sheet also has one bank unit F that the student fills with the printed two-digit form mark of the paper (serial 0 midterm A, 1 midterm B, 2 make-up A, 3 make-up B, plus its check digit); the reader reads it like any bank unit and the grading tool compares it with the key.

modules.role: sheet: specification, layout, renderer, check digit, registration, bubble features, naive reader
reader: read_sheet with optical-density flags; imports the v1_0_0 module

reuse.how_obtained: byte-identical vendored copies in 08-tooling of the SEN0414 repository (made by the engine task, not by this one), each with its SHA-256 recorded here and in a vendor record file; at control the copy and the source are compared byte for byte and with the recorded digest
reuse.if_source_changes: A source whose SHA-256 differs from the record means the sheet geometry, thresholds or reader changed after this design was written. The check fails; the vendored copy is not replaced by itself; a person decides whether to adopt the new version, and the sample sheet reading test is repeated before any paper is printed.

sample_run.folder: scratch folder outside the repository, not kept
not_measured: a printed sheet scanned or photographed
a scan at a resolution other than 150 dpi (the module expects its own frame; a scan must be resized to 150 dpi first)

choice.options: given by the specification, ABCD here

match.options: given by the specification, ABCDEFG here

bank.options: digits 0 to 9 in each row; the two digits are a serial and its Damm check digit

human.options: a box of digit cells written by hand; the reader only sees ink and holds the unit for a person

answer_sheet.units_per_sub_question: one unit per sub-question: choice for mcq and predict, match for a match premise, order for an order step, bank for a blank or cloze gap; plus the form mark F

units.what: form mark (serial 0 midterm A, 1 midterm B, 2 make-up A, 3 make-up B and its check digit)

answer_sheet.read_by_machine_answers: every mcq and predict letter, every match premise, every order step, every bank code (blank and cloze), the form mark in unit F, and the closure row of each block
answer_sheet.held_for_a_person: the identification box; every row flagged double, faint, incomplete, check-digit or held-block; every sheet page the reader cannot register; every X-ed mark in doubt
answer_sheet.title_overprint: The title line SEN0401 answer sheet is covered on the rendered PDF by a white box with the SEN0414 text; the module is not edited (assumption A9).
answer_sheet.outputs: one PDF with its layout file (position-exact, built by the module), for both forms

key.docx: answer, points, reason, tip and chapter of every sub-question, in print order, editable
key.machine: JSON with, for every sheet unit, the answer and the points, a SHA-256 over its content, kind, form and version
key.points: the sub-question table; Q5 is reported on its own line; no negative marking
key.refusal: refused when kind, form and version differ from the form mark read in unit F

outputs.sheet: answer sheet PDF and layout JSON

grading.read_by_machine: The module's reader reads every choice, match, order and bank row and the closure rows; filled from a mean ink of 0.50, faint from 0.12 (or optical density 0.03 below that), struck by ink in at least three of four corner patches.
grading.read_by_hand: The identification box, every held row, every sheet page that cannot be registered and any doubted X-ed mark; the person's reading of the original sheet is final.
grading.unreadable_rule: A sheet page is held when fewer than three corner marks are found; a bank unit is held when its rows are incomplete, doubled or faint or its code fails the check digit; a block is held whole when its closure row disagrees with its blank rows; a held item is never scored by the machine.
grading.double_mark_rule: A row with two or more filled bubbles is held; a person decides from the original sheet, taking an X-ed bubble as withdrawn; if the person cannot decide the row scores zero; an empty row scores zero.
grading.key_application: One key file per paper and form (answer and points of every position, with a SHA-256 digest of its content); refused when kind, form and version differ from the form mark read in unit F; points: mcq 3, predict 4, match 1 per premise, order 1 per step, blank 1 per gap, cloze 1 per gap; total 100; no negative marking.
grading.second_check: The module's read_sheet and read_naive must agree per row or the row is held; the total is recomputed by a second routine; a person compares original and result for every held sheet and a random sample of at least 10 per cent of sheets and at least 5.

decided.decision: Five questions: Q1 to Q4 of 25 points, Q5 of 10 points as a bonus; the cover page is filled from the supplied template; 4 pages if it fits, otherwise 6 with better formatting.
decided.reason: The Owner's words of 13:04 Istanbul, recorded as relayed in the brief.

decided.decision: No memorisation questions; terms get a tip; abbreviations are spelled out at first use; sub-questions ask about use, reason or effect.
decided.reason: The Owner's words of 13:04; for SEN0414 read as not syntax trivia.

decided.decision: The answer sheet is a position-exact PDF built by the SEN0401 sheet module.
decided.reason: The coordinator accepted this on 2026-11-01 as the SEN0401 owner chose.

decided.decision: Physical printed paper of one 60-minute sitting; code on paper is read-and-choose plus fill-the-blank; page-interactive questions are seeds and never copied.
decided.reason: The Owner's statement of 2026-10-30, still holding.
decided.effect: time rule, item types, near-copy rule

assumptions.assumption: A match premise and an order step are each one sub-question (so Q3 has 5 + 2 and Q4 has 4 + 2).
assumptions.if_other: If a whole match block or order block were one sub-question, Q3 would have 3 and Q4 3 sub-questions and the total 30 could not be reached with the brief's 7 and 6; Q3 and Q4 would need seven and six separate blocks and the paper would grow by about 40 lines.

assumptions.assumption: Chapter weights 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 4, 4, 3 (the lineage defaults reduced by one in chapters 2, 3 and 4).
assumptions.if_other: Any other weights summing to 30 change only the chapter matrix and the choice of seeds; time, points and the sheet do not change.

assumptions.assumption: Chapter 5 is asked only in Q2, Q3 and Q4.
assumptions.if_other: Putting it in Q1 needs a listing about debugging with a traceback; the page estimate rises by about 10 lines.

assumptions.assumption: Bloom reading 'Apply and above' = levels 3 to 6 for the majority rule, and 'Analyze and above' = levels 4 to 6 for the 8-of-30 rule, both also by points.
assumptions.if_other: If the majority rule meant Analyze and above, 11 of 30 (37 per cent) would fail it; at least 16 sub-questions at levels 4 to 6 would be needed, i.e. most of Q2 and Q3 would have to become why-questions.

assumptions.assumption: The allowances: 10 s per tip, 30 s per shared text, 120 s cover, 8 s per sheet unit.
assumptions.if_other: They add 818 s in all; the sub-questions alone take 1812 s, so 1428 s of the 3240 s are free for allowances: they could be 1.7 times as large before the 90 per cent rule fails.

assumptions.assumption: Term, date and time are inputs to the Papers task and are not decided here.
assumptions.if_other: If the engine had to default them, a wrong date would be printed on every paper.

assumptions.assumption: Program outcomes are left as a dash because the repository has none; learning outcomes per question come from 01-outcomes/sen0414_outcomes_v1_0_0.ttl, which says it is a draft that fills an empty catalogue page.
assumptions.if_other: If the department supplies program outcomes, the cover's row is filled by a one-line input; nothing else changes.

assumptions.assumption: The bonus adds to the total (up to 110).
assumptions.if_other: If the total is capped at 100, the mark of a student with a perfect Q1 to Q4 gains nothing from Q5; the cover's total row changes to 'at most 100'.

assumptions.assumption: The sheet title is overprinted to read SEN0414.
assumptions.if_other: If accepted as it is, the sheet says SEN0401; if overprinted, one more engine step and one look by a person.
A match or order bonus would add sheet units of another kind and about 10 lines.
